newsitem.title: USA: Compaq unveils new server line.
newsitem.headline: Compaq unveils new server line.

text.p: Compaq Computer Corp on Monday unveiled its new line of servers that feature a technology designed to keep the systems running all the time.
The servers, called the Compaq ProLiant 7000 and Compaq ProLiant 6500, are designed to target the high-end of the market.
They cost a minimum of just under $17,000 and just under $15,000, respectively, said John Rose, senior vice president and general manager of the company's enterprise computing group.
In a telephone interview, Rose said one of the most competitive features of the servers are its "hot plug PCI technology," also known as fault-tolerant technology.

This technology, developed by Compaq, keeps the servers running all the time, even if a part of the system needs to be replaced. Rose said its servers are the first in the industry to feature this technology.
Rose said Intel Corp on Friday announced that it had licensed this technology from Compaq. Compaq therefore expects the technology to eventually be found in competitive systems, he said.
In a written statement, Compaq said its servers run software applications that perform tasks such as transaction processing, decision support and corporate accounting .
Analysts said the PCI hot plug technology will likely help Compaq compete in the high-end market.
"The key here is availability, being able to keep the servers up at all time," said James Gruener, a senior analyst with Aberdeen Group Inc.
Compaq said its main competitors in the server market are Hewlett-Packard CO, Sun Microsystems Inc and International Business Machines Corp.
